market_context: U.S. equity futures were higher before the open, with Nasdaq futures up about 0.7%-0.8%, S&P 500 futures up about 0.3%-0.5%, and Dow futures up about 0.5%.[4][15] September payrolls were reported at 29,000 versus approximately 90,000 expected, while unemployment rose to 4.2%; Treasury yields and oil prices fell, supporting rate-sensitive technology shares but raising concerns about economic growth.[6][8] Nike fell roughly 9%-10% premarket after weak results and guidance, while ON Semiconductor, Microchip Technology, Intel, and other semiconductor-related shares were among notable premarket gainers.[2][3]

Nasdaq futures rose approximately 0.6%-0.8% ahead of trading, outperforming S&P and Dow futures, while lower yields generally support long-duration technology valuations.[4][12][15] QQQ is therefore likely to outperform SPY, although the weak employment report could produce intraday volatility.

Semiconductor shares were prominent among premarket gainers, including ON Semiconductor, Microchip Technology, and Intel, while Nasdaq futures were strongly positive.[3][4] This provides a favorable sector read-through for NVDA, but the stock-specific prediction is less certain because no direct NVDA catalyst was identified.
